description: Standalone guest examples with exact expected stdout. 'current' uses only the TS-001 syntax subset; 'deferred' needs later features and is not a current regression.

examples.rule: A closure retains and shares its captured binding; it sees later assignments.
Each call creates a fresh environment; closures from one call share it, closures from different calls do not.
Bindings hold object references; mutation is shared through aliases, rebinding is not, and identity is not structural.
`this` comes from the call form: member calls (dot or computed) pass the object; plain calls pass undefined in strict code.

examples.rule: Arguments, operands, callee and assignment target/key are evaluated left to right before the right-hand side; && and || short-circuit.

examples.rule: Names resolve to the nearest enclosing binding; inner bindings and assignments to them do not affect outer bindings.
A while condition (with its side effects) runs before every iteration; continue re-tests it, break does not.
return exits the whole function from any nesting depth; missing or bare return yields undefined; inner returns stay inner.

examples.rule: Function declarations are initialized before their scope's statements run, enabling calls before the declaration and mutual recursion.
for-let creates a binding per iteration; var shares one binding across all closures.
finally always runs; a normal finally preserves the earlier completion, an abrupt one replaces it.
Arrow functions use the enclosing function's this regardless of how they are called; ordinary functions do not.
